objective: Decide the r = 2 dichotomy for counting maps from closed 3-manifold groups with H1(M; F_p) = 0 into G = N x| C2, N of exponent p and class c < p with an involution theta, n = n+ + n-. Conjecture: polynomial iff the Lie triple system n- is abelian ([[n-, n-], n-] = 0), #P-hard otherwise. Prove the polynomial side for every class; prove hardness where the gadget calculus of BEYOND-CLASS2-20261027-001C extends; measure steering for class-3 and class-4 groups under a frozen contract; record the precise gap. Approved by the owner on 2026-10-27 ('Yes, please continue') after the past-class-2 epic.
status: Complete: the r = 2 dichotomy holds through class 4. Counting maps from closed 3-manifolds with H1(M; F_p) = 0 into N x| C2 is polynomial iff the Lie triple system n- is abelian (A, every class) and #P-hard otherwise (C, graded, class at most 4, on 2-surgeries of knots; steering supported by B). Next (the general coprime dichotomy for every r, 2/3) awaits the owner.
stop_rule: Stop when the dichotomy is proved for a stated range of classes (both sides) or a substantive obstruction to the route is found; report the criterion and its precise gaps.
title: Counting maps to p-group-by-involution groups: does the Lie triple system decide?
